sections.h2: Where are Lee County, Florida property records recorded?
sections.html:
Lee County deeds, mortgages and other instruments are recorded by the Lee County Clerk of Court, through its Official Records Services office. The clerk takes documents at two counters: 2115 Second Street in Fort Myers and the Lee County Government Center at 1039 SE 9th Place in Cape Coral.

Mail goes to Lee County Clerk of Courts, PO Box 2278, Fort Myers, FL 33902. The clerk also accepts electronic recording, which the page describes as a secure online process that avoids mail, couriers and trips to the office. The clerk's office will not fill out forms for you, and its page suggests hiring a professional experienced in preparing deeds. That advice fits Lee County sales well, since a deed with a wrong legal description or a missing witness line is returned and delays the closing. The legal description must be accurate on every instrument, and the spelling of each name must match the signature block.

  • In person: Fort Myers or Cape Coral.
  • By mail: with a self-addressed stamped envelope.
  • Drop box: documents, payment and return envelope sealed together.
  • Electronic: through the clerk's E-Record service.

sections.h2: What must a Lee County deed contain to be recorded?
sections.html:
The clerk says a deed must meet the requirements of section 695.26 of the Florida Statutes, and its checklist is specific. A rejected deed costs time, so run through it before you sign.

  • A line naming and giving the address of whoever drafted the deed.
  • Printed names and mailing addresses of the grantors (sellers) and grantees (buyers).
  • Grantor signatures with names printed beneath them.
  • Two witnesses, with their names and addresses printed under their signatures.
  • A complete notary acknowledgment: names, date, notary signature, printed name, commission expiration and seal.
  • Blank space reserved at the top right corner: 3 by 3 inches on page one, 1 by 3 inches on later pages.

The clerk adds that any document transferring property needs two witnesses for each signature, though a corporation signs with its seal in place of witnesses. The sale price or consideration must appear on the deed or in a cover letter, since the clerk needs it to compute tax. The Florida statute on conveyances also asks for two subscribing witnesses on a deed of land.

sections.h2: How much does the Lee County clerk charge to record?
sections.html:
On letter or legal paper, Lee's clerk prints $10.00 for page one and $8.50 for every page after it. Indexing adds $1.00 for every name beyond four.

Behind those totals is a statutory base of $5.00 and $4.00 under section 28.24(13), with extra charges added. The clerk's own page is the number to plan around. A document short on blank space at the top right can draw a charge for an extra page, a cost that is easy to avoid.

sections.h2: What taxes apply when a Lee County deed or mortgage is recorded?
sections.html:
Doc stamps come due when the deed is recorded: 70 cents for each $100, or part of $100, on warranty deeds, quit claim deeds and similar transfers. The clerk takes the money and passes it to the Department of Revenue.

Mortgages are different. The clerk's page says intangible tax on a note secured by a mortgage is paid at recording at 2 mills, or $.002 per dollar of the amount financed. The Department of Revenue adds that mortgage and note documentary stamps run 35 cents per $100 of the amount secured, with a $2,450 cap on a note and no cap on a mortgage.

On who pays, the state says all parties to a document are liable whichever one agrees to pay. Most Lee County purchase contracts assign the deed stamps to the seller, but the contract is where that gets decided. State guidance lists an estate representative's deed under a probated will as not taxable, and exempts a divorce deed for the marital home.

sections.h2: Does the Lee County clerk record death certificates and other documents?
sections.html:
Yes, with rules. The clerk says an uncertified copy of a death certificate cannot be recorded unless a court or the Attorney General deems otherwise. A Florida death certificate presented for recording must be a certified copy approved by the Department of Health that leaves out confidential cause-of-death details, and one that includes cause of death will not be recorded.

Non-Florida death certificates must be certified copies issued by that state's agencies or courts. Heirs who plan to sell a parent's Lee County house often need this paper, so order a recordable version up front. Order several copies, because the county keeps the one it records and a title company may want another for its file. Ask the Florida Department of Health, not the clerk, how to get the version that omits cause of death.

Other requirements apply to all recordings. Names must be spelled the same in the body and under each signature. Anything that moves an interest in real property, except mortgages, must show the grantee's mailing address. The page lists exceptions to these formatting rules, including wills, plats, court orders and instruments signed outside Florida. If you mail documents without a stamped return envelope, the clerk holds them, and the page says anything still held after 90 days is destroyed.

sections.h2: What do Lee County foreclosure and eviction filings cost, and where do they show up?
sections.html:
Foreclosure and other real property cases cost $470.00 below $50,000, $975.00 from $50,000 to $250,000 and $1,975.00 above $250,000 to file, according to the clerk's fee page. The clerk charges $70.00 to hold the judicial sale and asks a $600.00 deposit for the notice of sale.

A recorded lis pendens warns buyers that a suit touches the parcel. By statute the sale follows judgment by 20 to 35 days, and an electronic auction is allowed. A homeowner behind on a mortgage has the option of a pre-sale deal that clears the loan from the proceeds.

Tenant eviction filings in county court cost $185.00, and the sheriff's fee for a writ of possession is listed at $90.00, subject to change by the sheriff. Landlords selling a rented Lee County house should expect a buyer to ask for lease copies, so pull those before listing. Buyers also ask whether any tenant has received a notice, and the answer should match what the court docket shows.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in Lee County, Florida?
faqs.a: The Lee County Clerk of Court records deeds through its Official Records Services office. You can record in Fort Myers, in Cape Coral, by mail, in a drop box or electronically.

faqs.q: How many witnesses does a Lee County deed need?
faqs.a: Two. The clerk's checklist calls for two witnesses with printed names and addresses, plus a full notary acknowledgment, and it adds a prepared-by statement and mailing addresses for the sellers and buyers.

faqs.q: What is the Lee County recording fee?
faqs.a: Standard recording is $10.00 for page one and $8.50 for the rest, and each name over four costs $1.00 more. Deed documentary stamps are charged separately at $0.70 per $100.00.

faqs.q: Can I record an uncertified death certificate in Lee County?
faqs.a: No, unless a court or the Attorney General says otherwise. The certificate must be certified, and a Florida one must exclude confidential cause-of-death information.

faqs.q: Will the Lee County clerk return my recorded document by mail?
faqs.a: Only if you include a self-addressed stamped envelope. Without one the clerk holds the document, and the clerk's page says anything held more than 90 days is destroyed.
